title: Letrozole · daily hormone therapy
context_label: Postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer; setting-specific pathways
schedule_summary: Take letrozole once daily continuously. The prescriber confirms whether the aim is before surgery, after surgery, extended adjuvant treatment or advanced-disease control.
purpose: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.
indication_text: Postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer in the specific NCCP early, extended, advanced or neoadjuvant indications. Neoadjuvant use has additional HER2-negative and treatment-suitability criteria; it is not inferred for every ER-positive cancer.
administration_text: Take with or without food. Take a forgotten dose when remembered unless the next dose is within about two to three hours; then skip it. Do not take two doses together.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile; confirm menopause with hormone tests when uncertain. Assess fracture risk and baseline bone density, particularly for adjuvant AI treatment. The NICE adjuvant baseline-DXA recommendation has an exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. FBC, renal / liver profile and lipids when clinically indicated. Review bone density during treatment and after treatment according to bone risk. Neoadjuvant response and surgical planning need explicit review milestones.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.mechanism: Reduces the oestrogen available to stimulate cancer cells
agents.explanation: After menopause, much of the body’s oestrogen is made when aromatase converts other hormones in fat and other tissues. Blocking that enzyme lowers oestrogen signalling in hormone-sensitive breast cancer. It does not reliably switch off functioning ovaries: ovarian suppression, if needed, must be prescribed and checked separately.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning may cause no early symptoms, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.
risks: Joint and muscle pain or stiffness
Hot flushes, sleep disturbance and fatigue
Uncommon liver abnormalities or serious allergic reactions

urgent_extra: Report persistent limiting joint pain, new severe bone pain or a possible fracture, jaundice, or new vaginal bleeding. New breast changes during preoperative treatment need review rather than waiting for the planned end date.

sections.title: Check the prescribed frequency
sections.text: The usual schedule is daily. In severe hepatic impairment NCCP specifies every other day; follow the individual prescription and do not make this change yourself.

sections.title: If treatment is before surgery
sections.text: Ask when response will be assessed, which team owns the surgical review and what would lead to earlier surgery or a different treatment.

sections.title: After surgery or previous tamoxifen
sections.text: Confirm whether this is the initial adjuvant course or an extension. Record the planned review date and previous endocrine-treatment duration.

sections.title: Support during treatment
sections.text: Keep the fracture-risk and DXA plan, discuss activity and joint symptoms, and check all medicines and supplements with the treating team.

evidence.title: BIG 1-98: letrozole as adjuvant therapy
evidence.population: 8,010 postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer; monotherapy comparison 4,922, letrozole versus tamoxifen for 5 years.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival including recurrence, second primaries and death; monotherapy median follow-up 8.7 years.
evidence.interpretation: Intention-to-treat DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.96); OS HR 0.87 (0.77–0.999). Sequential schedules did not significantly improve outcomes over letrozole alone.
evidence.limitations: 619 tamoxifen participants crossed to letrozole; crossover-adjusted estimates differ from intention-to-treat and must not be mixed. This is adjuvant evidence, not a benefit estimate for neoadjuvant or metastatic treatment.

additional_evidence.title: MA.17: extended adjuvant letrozole after tamoxifen
additional_evidence.population: 5,187 postmenopausal women after 5 years of tamoxifen; planned 5 years letrozole versus placebo.
additional_evidence.interpretation: At 30 months median follow-up, DFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.76); distant DFS HR 0.60 (0.43–0.84). Overall OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.82,0.57–1.19).
additional_evidence.limitations: Stopped early for benefit. Supports a specific post-tamoxifen extension strategy, not indefinite treatment or automatic extension after every previous AI course.

additional_evidence.title: P 024: neoadjuvant letrozole
additional_evidence.population: 337 postmenopausal women with untreated ER/PgR-positive primary breast cancer, initially unsuitable for breast-conserving surgery; 4 months letrozole versus tamoxifen.
additional_evidence.interpretation: Clinical response 55% versus 36%; breast-conserving surgery 45% versus 35%.
additional_evidence.limitations: Short preoperative response study, not a survival trial. Clinical reassessment and surgical planning remain essential; the trial duration must not override NCCP's individualized 4–8 month neoadjuvant window.

teachback: What is your treatment schedule, which checks apply to your setting, and who books and reviews them?
consent_support: NCCP Child-Pugh C dosing is 2.5 mg every other day; this is not the same hepatic advice as anastrozole. The daily schedule shown is the usual dose and must be checked against the prescription. AIs alone require a confirmed postmenopausal endocrine state. Ovarian suppression is a separate treatment plan and must not be assumed from this card.

support.title: Symptoms and daily life
support.text: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning may cause no early symptoms, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: No routine antiemetic, steroid premedication or G-CSF is required by this endocrine monotherapy. Ask for individual symptom support.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Ask who books each check, when it is due and who reviews it. Tell the team if an expected appointment has not arrived.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.

items.title: Who this card covers
items.text: Postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer in the specific NCCP early, extended, advanced or neoadjuvant indications. Neoadjuvant use has additional HER2-negative and treatment-suitability criteria; it is not inferred for every ER-positive cancer.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 2.5 mg orally once daily. Take with or without food. Take a forgotten dose when remembered unless the next dose is within about two to three hours; then skip it. Do not take two doses together.

items.title: Duration and decision points
items.text: For the NCCP neoadjuvant pathway, reassess response during a four-to-eight-month course and discuss surgery or alternatives if response is inadequate. Adjuvant / extended duration and advanced-disease continuation follow separate plans.

items.title: Individual safety
items.text: NCCP Child-Pugh C dosing is 2.5 mg every other day; this is not the same hepatic advice as anastrozole. The daily schedule shown is the usual dose and must be checked against the prescription.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Baseline, ongoing safety checks and cancer scans have different purposes.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile; confirm menopause with hormone tests when uncertain. Assess fracture risk and baseline bone density, particularly for adjuvant AI treatment. The NICE adjuvant baseline-DXA recommendation has an exception for patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: FBC, renal / liver profile and lipids when clinically indicated. Review bone density during treatment and after treatment according to bone risk. Neoadjuvant response and surgical planning need explicit review milestones.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for letrozole alone. Assess cardiovascular risk factors and new symptoms as clinically indicated.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Offer baseline DXA when starting an adjuvant aromatase inhibitor if not already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates; assess fracture risk and relevant previous results. Under the 2025 joint guidance, patients with a T-score above −2.0 and no additional risk factors generally have risk and bone density reassessed every one to two years. Patients on bone-protective treatment generally have BMD reassessed about every two years. Fracture, substantial bone loss or a change in risk can require earlier review. The clinician selects the interval and any bone treatment; these are not automatic yearly scans for everyone.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After curative treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy
items.text: In an early-breast pathway, chemotherapy, if indicated, precedes endocrine treatment. Surgery and its pathology guide adjuvant choices. Postoperative radiotherapy is usually delivered after recovery and any adjuvant chemotherapy; aromatase inhibitors may overlap radiotherapy under the agreed plan. Tamoxifen timing around radiotherapy is agreed by the treating teams. None of these additional treatments is automatically required by an endocrine prescription.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: AIs alone require a confirmed postmenopausal endocrine state. Ovarian suppression is a separate treatment plan and must not be assumed from this card.

chapters.title: Evidence for a different decision
chapters.intro: Each study applies to its own population and treatment setting.

items.title: MA.17: extended adjuvant letrozole after tamoxifen
items.text: 5,187 postmenopausal women after 5 years of tamoxifen; planned 5 years letrozole versus placebo. At 30 months median follow-up, DFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.76); distant DFS HR 0.60 (0.43–0.84). Overall OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.82,0.57–1.19). Stopped early for benefit. Supports a specific post-tamoxifen extension strategy, not indefinite treatment or automatic extension after every previous AI course.

items.title: P 024: neoadjuvant letrozole
items.text: 337 postmenopausal women with untreated ER/PgR-positive primary breast cancer, initially unsuitable for breast-conserving surgery; 4 months letrozole versus tamoxifen. Clinical response 55% versus 36%; breast-conserving surgery 45% versus 35%. Short preoperative response study, not a survival trial. Clinical reassessment and surgical planning remain essential; the trial duration must not override NCCP's individualized 4–8 month neoadjuvant window.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.
